function: Joint learned AP precoding and RIS phase-shift design (heterogeneous-agent RL) maximizing downlink sum spectral efficiency in RIS-aided cell-free massive MIMO. p. 1-3
system: Cell-free mMIMO downlink: L=9 APs with M=2-16 antennas, K=6 single-antenna UEs, R=8 reflecting RISs with N=4-64 elements, 1.9 GHz, 1 km x 1 km. p. 2, p. 4-5
method: Heterogeneous-agent trust region policy optimization (HATRPO) multi-agent reinforcement learning; each AP and RIS an agent, actor-critic, centralized training with decentralized execution, local CSI only. p. 2-4
data_channel: Own simulator, no dataset: i.i.d. Rayleigh fading (p. 2); three-slope large-scale fading with 8 dB log-normal shadowing, 1 km x 1 km area, 1.9 GHz (p. 4)
test_conditions: Training curves for L=9, M=4, K=6, R=8, N=16 (2500 episodes); sum-SE then reported while sweeping AP antennas M=2-16 and RIS elements N=4-64; retraining per setting not stated. p. 4-5
baselines: Non-learned: MMSE (theoretical reference), genetic algorithm [6]. Learned: MAPPO, MADDPG (MARL algorithms on the same problem); DDPG [22] appears only in the CSI-interaction count. p. 4-5
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency (bit/s/Hz) versus AP antennas and RIS elements; average reward versus training episode; CSI interaction count; training time per episode. p. 4-5
complexity: Big-O order of HATRPO given in L, M, K, R, N, layer sizes and SE cost, compared with MADDPG; training time per episode 235-1973 ms (Table I). p. 4-5
openness: none; own simulator, no code or data link in the paper. p. 4
q1_support: p. 4: "The large-scale fading coefficients are generated using a three-slope propagation model with log-normal shadow fading". Missing: no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel; p. 2 assumes "independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Rayleigh fading channel".
q2_support: p. 4: "Average reward against the training episode with L = 9, M = 4, K = 6, R = 8, and N = 16." Missing: no statement that trained agents are tested with other M, N, K or in another scenario; Figs. 3-4 sweep M and N without saying whether the agents are retrained or reused.
q3_support: p. 5: "HATRPO outperforms the genetic algorithm (GA) proposed in [6] by 34.52%, MADDPG by 19.24% and MAPPO by 11.68%"
q4_support: p. 4: "We compare the computational complexity of different algorithms." The paragraph gives the order O(L^2 M K R^2 N^2 sum Q_a^2 + ...) for HATRPO and for MADDPG; p. 5, Table I: "Average training time of proposed algorithm per episode (ms)"
q5_support: p. 4: "The large-scale fading coefficients are generated using a three-slope propagation model with log-normal shadow fading". Missing: no code or data link or release statement, and no public dataset or measured data (own simulator).
notes: Included, area 3: learned joint AP precoding and RIS phase-shift design (p. 1-3). The RIS is a passive reflecting RIS: |phi| <= 1 in Eq. 2 and phase in [0, 2 pi] in Eq. 10 (p. 2-3). q1: channels are i.i.d. Rayleigh (p. 2) with a three-slope large-scale model and 8 dB log-normal shadowing (p. 4), a custom simulator; no 3GPP model, dataset or measurement is named. The paper is not consistent on this point: Algorithm 1 line 6 says it generates a spatially correlated channel (p. 4) while the system model assumes i.i.d. Rayleigh (p. 2). q2: training is shown at L=9, M=4, K=6, R=8, N=16 (Fig. 2); Figs. 3-4 sweep M and N, but the paper never says whether the agents are retrained or reused, so it is not met. q3: non-learned MMSE benchmark and GA [6]; learned MAPPO and MADDPG, all compared on sum-SE (p. 5). q4: order of complexity of HATRPO and MADDPG (p. 4) and measured training time per episode (Table I, p. 5). q5: no code or data link; own simulator. The extracted text of pages 3 and 4 is interleaved, so pages 2 to 5 were also viewed as page images (Table I, Figs. 2-4, complexity expressions).
